calls.reason: A Morgan Stanley analyst did press Microsoft on capex ROI in January 2026, which fits the forecast. But nothing in the packet shows the claimed negative AI returns, and Microsoft's broad earnings growth doesn't settle that either way.

Oracle says its AI capacity earned a 32% gross margin, which cuts against the no-profit premise. But that is the company's own figure and only a gross margin. The packet has no evidence on full cost recovery, and the six-year window is still open.
The packet has no legal ruling on the deals and no deal-level evidence on whether they can last. CoreWeave's backlog and Lambda's funding are only context.

The Register traces the roughly $8.7B figure back to Zitron's own leaked documents. It describes it as Azure-only spending for January–September, and Microsoft said the numbers weren't quite right. No independent record confirms the amount or the period.
CoreWeave clearly borrowed to buy equipment. But OpenAI's credit line was undrawn when it opened, and Anthropic raised $13B in equity, so the evidence on debt reliance across both levels is mixed.

None of the four companies reports AI-specific profit. AWS profits and Meta's claim that AI is already paying off in its core business are suggestive but don't settle either the zero-profit claim or the $1.21T gap.
